pure-announcement.rationale: This is a podcast episode recap of a practitioner interview on observability practice, not a product launch, release note, or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: The supplied nearest concepts are all MCP-, graph-, and agent-governance notes; none covers Observability 2.0, cardinality economics, or the three-pillars critique discussed here.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The claims are attributed on the record to Charity Majors with links to the full episode, transcript, and her published writing, so a reader can check both the source and the argument.

durability.rationale: The load-bearing ideas — the three-pillars model multiplying storage cost, high cardinality driving observability spend, unified structured-event storage, SLOs as the entry point, OTel for vendor portability — are mechanisms and trade-offs that will hold in twelve months even if side remarks like DevOps's decline date.

actionability.rationale: It is a timestamped episode summary that states positions ('dashboards are a poor view', 'SLOs are the APIs for teams', 'move to 80% structured data') at survey level across a dozen topics without enough mechanism on any one of them for a reader to act.

atomicity.rationale: A dominant thesis (Observability 2.0: unified high-cardinality event storage replacing the three pillars) carries most of the note, but it is bundled with separable riders on DevOps's obsolescence, Honeycomb's custom database, mobile observability, and AI-code observability.
